lead.headline: The AI Trade Cracks Again: Chip Stocks Lose Nearly 8% in New York and Asia's Chip Markets Erase Tuesday's Record Rebound
lead.dek: One day after Jensen Huang's reinstatement sparked the biggest one-day gain in Nvidia's history, investors sold semiconductors hard, rotated into value and healthcare, and pushed the Dow above 50,000 while the Nasdaq fell 1.5%.
body: The relief rally that followed Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang lasted one session. On Tuesday 24 November the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell nearly 8%, the Nasdaq Composite lost 1.48% to 23,733.54 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,201.09, its eighth loss in nine sessions. Nvidia gave back about 6%, Micron 11%, and AMD, Intel and Applied Materials 7-9%. Analog Devices sank 17.4% after a cautious outlook and Hewlett Packard Enterprise 16.3%.

Money did not leave the market so much as change seats. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, healthcare led the sector table, and Kohl's (+19.5%), Dollar Tree (+11.2%), Nike (about +6%) and Moderna (+7.2%) rallied. Sanofi's $41 billion agreement to buy Insmed added to the defensive bid. US consumer confidence also surprised to the upside, with the Conference Board index jumping to 103.3 against a 92.2 forecast.

The reversal hit Asia harder on Wednesday morning. Taiwan's Taiex fell as much as 7.9% and South Korea's Kospi more than 6%, a day after both posted record rebounds; Japan's Nikkei 225 was down about 2.8% by the afternoon. Tokyo Electron dropped 13.5%, Advantest 14.5%, Samsung Electronics 9.1%, SK Hynix 9.9%, and TSMC and Foxconn more than 9% each. Hong Kong was the exception, edging higher.

Reports cited doubts that technology groups can keep funding multi-trillion-dollar AI spending (Gartner puts AI-related investment at $2.7 trillion this year and $3.6 trillion in 2027), expectations of a regulatory push after the US midterms, and fresh Washington scrutiny of Huang, who faces closed-door House interviews on 1 December and a public Senate hearing on 3 December. Reports that the US may unveil new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and others as soon as this week added to the caution before today's US PCE inflation and GDP data.

impact.title: What it means for markets
points: Leadership is narrowing again: the S&P 500 fell while the Dow rose, a sign that investors are cutting AI-hardware exposure rather than equities as a whole. Equal-weight and value indices benefit relative to cap-weighted tech benchmarks.

Asia's chip-heavy markets (Taiex, Kospi, Nikkei) remain the highest-beta expression of the AI trade; Korea's expected rate hike on Thursday and Taiwan's short-selling curbs are now being tested in a falling tape.
The rotation favours defensives and healthcare (Sanofi, Lilly, J&J higher) and US retailers that beat forecasts; memory and analog chipmakers carry the heaviest estimate risk.
Today's PCE print matters more than usual: a December Fed hike is almost fully priced, so an upside surprise would hit long-duration growth stocks just as AI sentiment is fragile.

read.title: The Ledger's Read
paragraphs: Monday's Huang relief rally was a short-covering event, not a change of view. By Tuesday investors were again selling the most crowded AI hardware names, from Nvidia and Micron to Analog Devices, and by Wednesday Asia's chip-heavy markets had handed back their record gains. What is notable is where the money went: the Dow closed above 50,000, healthcare and value retail rallied, and Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed deal underlined appetite for defensive growth. This is rotation more than retreat.

Rates are the second front. A December Fed hike is all but priced, inflation prints from Australia and Japan came in hot, and Korea is expected to raise rates on Thursday. Today's US PCE and GDP data therefore matter for the second hike, not the first: a firm print would pressure long-duration tech just as AI sentiment is fragile, while a soft one could extend the bond rally that took the 10-year to a two-week low.

Geopolitics is adding layered risk rather than a single shock. Oil remains oversupplied, but each Hormuz mine claim lifts Brent by a few dollars; Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports widen the shipping risk map; and new Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies would hit the same Asian exporters now absorbing the chip sell-off. Watch PCE at 14:30 CET, the Bank of Korea overnight, and Huang's hearings next week.

body: Tuesday split the US market in two. The Dow added 0.85% to finish at 50,018.70 while the cap-weighted S&P 500 lost 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.48%. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell nearly 8%, undoing much of Monday's surge after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang.

Earnings did the work on the upside. Kohl's rose 19.48% and Dollar Tree 11.18% after both beat forecasts; Dollar Tree lifted its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $8.05-8.25. Nike gained nearly 6% and Moderna 7.2%. On the downside Analog Devices lost 17.37% on a cautious first-quarter outlook, HPE 16.31% and Micron 11%.

Data helped the consumer names: the Conference Board's November confidence index rose to 103.3, 11.4 points above October and well ahead of the 92.2 consensus, while the University of Michigan's sentiment gauge stood at 51.5.

After the bell Dell edged up about 1% and HP fell about 3% (Saxo). With Thanksgiving on Thursday and a half-day on Friday, Wednesday's PCE and GDP releases are the last major data before the Fed's 9 December meeting.

body: European stocks opened flat on Tuesday and drifted lower as the US chip sell-off took hold. The STOXX 600 closed down 0.7% at 632.74 after Monday's 1.8% rise, its best session in nearly a month. Frankfurt fared worst among the majors, with the DAX down 1.3% to 25,017.81.

Semiconductor stocks led the decline: Aixtron lost 16.3%, Infineon 9.7% and ASML 5.6%. Miners fell with copper, which slid to a 13-month low; Antofagasta dropped 8.1%. Sanofi rose 9.9% after agreeing to buy US drugmaker Insmed.

Germany's Ifo business climate rose to 90.6 in November from 90.1, matching forecasts and reaching its highest level since May 2023, though manufacturing sentiment slipped for the first time in seven months.
In bonds, Bund yields fell 2-3bp and gilt yields 1-3bp; the BTP-Bund spread widened 4bp to 109bp and the OAT-Bund spread 2bp to 152bp.

stories.headline: Sensex Jumps as Much as 1,916 Points as India Reopens After the Holiday, Then Pares Gains as Asia Slides
stories.summary: Indian shares caught up with Tuesday's global rebound when trading resumed on Wednesday 25 Nov after the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. By noon IST the Sensex was up 1,916 points (2.3%) at 84,352 and the Nifty 50 up 2.2% at 25,917; by 13:00 IST gains had narrowed to 1,356 points (1.6%) at 83,792 and 25,706. Oil-sensitive stocks such as CEAT rose up to 5% with Brent below $90, and insurers PB Fintech, Max Financial and HDFC Life up to 8%. APL Apollo Tubes slid another 19.6% to a 52-week low.
stories.market: Domestic catch-up buying met a falling Asian tape; metals lagged on the Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal and weaker copper.

body: India sat out Tuesday's trading for a holiday and reopened into a very different global mood. The Sensex still opened sharply higher, reflecting Monday's US rally, and peaked around midday with a gain of 1,916 points before trimming that to about 1,356 points by 13:00 IST as Asian chip stocks tumbled.

Leadership came from oil-sensitive and financial names. Tyre maker CEAT led gains of up to 5% among companies that benefit from cheaper crude, and insurers rallied up to 8% after Motilal Oswal reiterated a positive view. ABB India rose 2.5% after its parent agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, and Shadowfax gained 2.4% on a deal for WeFast.

Metals were the weak spot. APL Apollo Tubes fell 19.6% to Rs 1,342.20, extending Monday's crash, and Tata Steel lost 2.4% to Rs 159.06 even as its chairman said the company was reflecting on investor feedback. Piramal Pharma fell 7% after a block of about 100 million shares changed hands.

stories.headline: Treasuries Rally to a Two-Week Low in Yields as a December Fed Hike Stays Almost Fully Priced Before PCE
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 1.6bp to 4.932% on Tuesday 24 Nov, a two-week low, and the 2-year 0.7bp to 4.689%, while the 30-year rose 1.4bp to 5.323% (Saxo). CME FedWatch shows a December hike as almost certain, up from an 89% probability on Friday, with about a 5% chance of a 50bp move. New York Fed President John Williams said inflation is simply too high; the Fed's preferred gauge is running near 3.5%. October PCE and Q3 GDP are due today.
stories.market: The curve steepened at the long end as the front end held; a hot PCE print would lift the odds of a second hike in early 2027 and pressure long-duration equities.

body: Bond investors bought duration on Tuesday as equities wobbled. The 10-year yield ended near 4.93%, its lowest in two weeks, and the 2-year was little changed near 4.69%, while the 30-year rose to about 5.32%.

Policy pricing barely moved: futures treat a 25bp hike at the 9 December meeting as all but certain, and Reuters-reported pricing put the odds at about 97%. Aju Press, citing CME data, put a 66.9% probability on the funds rate reaching 4.25-4.50% by January.

The Fed's own messaging has hardened. Williams' warning that inflation is too high followed earlier comments leaving back-to-back moves on the table, and the preferred inflation gauge is near 3.5%, well above the 2% target.
Wednesday's October PCE and second Q3 GDP estimate are the last major data before the meeting; US markets then close for Thanksgiving.

body: Australia's October CPI rose 0.7% on the month and 4.9% on the year, above the 4.8% consensus, with electricity up 25.2% as rebates rolled off and fuel up 32.5%. The Bank of Korea decides on Thursday; all ten local brokerages surveyed expect a 25bp increase to 3.25% and most see a peak at 3.50%, with exports in the first 20 days of November up 101.5%.

stories.headline: Brent Rebounds 2.3% to $91.40 on New Hormuz Mine Claims After Its Lowest Close Since August
stories.summary: Brent settled up 2.3% at $91.40 a barrel on Tuesday 24 Nov and WTI 2.3% at $82.05, a day after Brent's lowest close since 31 Aug. Iran said more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claims no maritime authority has confirmed. Deutsche Bank estimates observed global inventories rose 52 million barrels in October, an oversupply of about 1.7 million b/d, and Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened. Brent eased to about $90.10 in Asian trade on Wednesday.
stories.market: The war premium is now traded headline by headline over an oversupplied physical market; energy equities and tanker rates swing with each strike report.

body: Oil spent Tuesday morning near three-month lows: Brent touched $88.71 in Asian trade and WTI $79.57, the lowest since late August. The tone changed after Iranian navy statements that two more tankers hit mines and caught fire east of the strait, and Brent settled 2.3% higher at $91.40.

Supply arguments still dominate. Deutsche Bank says observed liquids inventories rose 52 million barrels in October, consistent with an oversupply of 1.7 million b/d, and Libya's Sharara field resumed flows after a valve closure. DBS's Suvro Sarkar said Brent has lost upward momentum as supply stays benign, though stalled US-Iran talks leave rebound risk.
ANZ's Daniel Hynes described the market as moving from acute scarcity to persistent vulnerability, with thin buffers. Traffic through Hormuz remains a fraction of pre-war levels.
By Wednesday afternoon in Asia, Brent was about 1.4% lower near $90.10 and WTI near $80.72.

body: Copper's slide accelerated on Tuesday as the AI trade cracked. LME three-month metal closed at $11,826 a tonne, its lowest in 13 months, leaving it roughly 21% below September's record, the conventional threshold for a bear market. Comex futures fell 4.7%.

Equities tied to the metal fell hard: Antofagasta dropped 8.1%, Vale 5.5% (pulling the Ibovespa to a six-month low) and Grupo Mexico about 5.1%. Chile's IPSA fell 1.13% and the Chilean peso weakened to about 1,033 per dollar.

body: Gold could not hold Monday's bounce. The US close on Tuesday was about $3,556.85 and the metal drifted a further quarter-point lower in early Asia. Monday's gains had come as central banks bought the dip after gold's worst week since March.

With markets treating a December Fed hike as a done deal, gold's next move hinges on whether PCE pushes expectations toward a second hike; the Hormuz and Red Sea escalations are the main sources of haven demand.

stories.headline: Washington Readies New Section 301 Tariffs on 16 Economies Including China, the EU, Japan and India
stories.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to raise tariffs under a Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity, with an announcement possible as soon as this week, Bloomberg and the WSJ reported on 24 Nov. The probe covers 16 economies: China, the EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan and India. China is expected to face higher rates than others; the EU, Japan and South Korea 15% or lower; steel, aluminium and autos may be excluded because they already face Section 232 duties. The government had not confirmed the plans at press time.
stories.market: Adds to Asia's risk-off tone: exporters in Korea, Taiwan and Southeast Asia, the yuan and European autos are exposed; the yuan still touched a three-week high on Wednesday.

body: The US Trade Representative's Section 301 investigation into excess capacity covers 16 trading partners. Reports on 24 November said higher tariffs could be announced within days, with China facing the steepest increase.

When USTR first floated the measure on 2 June it proposed 10% for economies that adopt a forced-labour import ban and 12.5% for others. Trade lawyers expect China's overall rate to stay at or below 20% and the EU to remain under its 15% cap, with Section 232 sectors carved out.

Reuters noted the administration is poised to release findings of the probe as traders in Shanghai weighed the risk; the yuan nonetheless rose to 6.6581 per dollar on Wednesday, helped by exporter conversion.

stories.summary: US officials are investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 commercial vessels carrying oil, LPG and chemicals near the US, Europe and Asia, the Wall Street Journal reported on 23 Nov. Iran is the main suspect and Russia is also being considered, but investigators have not established responsibility. The attackers reportedly exploited vulnerabilities in Fortinet routers.
stories.market: A new risk channel for tanker operators and marine insurers beyond physical attacks; maritime cybersecurity and router vendors face scrutiny.

body: The probe widens the Iran war's reach into commercial shipping far from the Gulf. Ships affected were reported near US, European and Asian coasts.

stories.headline: Iran War, Day 271: Tehran Claims More Mine Strikes on Tankers and Sets Seven Conditions for Talks as Hormuz Traffic Falls 40%
stories.summary: Iran's navy said two tankers hit mines east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire on the morning of 24 Nov, after the IRGC said three 'violating' tankers were mined on Monday; UKMTO says projectiles struck three vessels with all crew accounted for, and no maritime authority has confirmed the mine account. Weekly crossings fell from 226 (1-7 Nov) to 125 (17-23 Nov), per MarineTraffic. Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Ghalibaf ruled out talks until seven conditions are met, including lifting the US naval blockade, while Qatar said contacts continue. Brent rose 2.3% to $91.40.
stories.market: Oil's war premium is reasserting itself only intermittently over a supply glut; war-risk insurance, tanker rates and Gulf equities remain the most sensitive channels.

body: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports, first imposed in April, lifted after June's memorandum of understanding and reinstated weeks later, has largely halted Iran's oil exports. Tehran's foreign ministry says it will not tolerate it, and Iran's army chief called for tighter control of the strait, with the IRGC navy warning ships off unapproved routes.

Accounts of the latest incidents conflict. Iranian outlets reported two tankers on fire on Tuesday morning after three on Monday; Lloyd's List and Riviera identified three Sinokor VLCCs attacked while exiting, and UKMTO reported projectile strikes with all crew safe. Al Jazeera counted more than 25 tankers hit in the past week.

Diplomacy is stuck. Ghalibaf's seven conditions include lifting the blockade, easing sanctions, releasing frozen funds and formally ending the war. Qatar's prime minister met Secretary of State Rubio on Monday, and Doha said on Tuesday that contacts continue and the strait must reopen. Trump has suggested US strikes could resume after the new year.

Washington is also widening its pressure: Treasury sanctioned 22 entities and 8 people in an Iranian shadow-banking network on Monday, and US investigators are examining possible Iranian cyberattacks on up to 50 ships.

stories.headline: Houthi Drone Hits Riyadh's PIF Tower for the Second Time in Five Days; Group Threatens Jeddah and All Saudi Red Sea Ports
stories.summary: A Houthi drone struck the PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district, home to the Public Investment Fund, on 24 Nov, injuring 11 people, Saudi civil defence said; it was the second strike on the building since 19 Nov. On 25 Nov the Houthis said Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports would be targeted if Saudi Arabia attacks Hodeidah, and told shipping firms to pull vessels. The Saudi-led coalition struck targets in Hodeidah, Saada and Amran, and Yemen's army says the Houthis are about 60 km from Aden. Britain sanctioned the Houthis and four officials.
stories.market: Direct threats to Saudi Red Sea ports raise war-risk costs for Red Sea shipping and the Yanbu export route; Saudi equities held up, with TASI +0.4% on Tuesday.

body: The escalation began in September when the Houthis advanced toward Bab el-Mandeb, and has since included strikes on Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, met by intensified Saudi air raids.
Hodeidah is the main entry point for food and fuel into Houthi-held northern Yemen, so strikes there carry humanitarian as well as shipping consequences.

stories.headline: Putin Vows 'Inevitable' Retaliation for Refinery Strikes That Have Cut Russian Processing by 45%, as Zelensky Eyes the New Congress
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin told oil executives on 24 Nov that Ukraine keeps hitting Russian refineries despite Trump's request to stop and that retaliation is inevitable. Two industry sources told Reuters Ukrainian drone strikes have cut combined Russian refinery throughput by 45% since late October, and several regions have restricted retail fuel sales. Zelensky said that if Trump's diplomacy fails by year-end Kyiv will turn to the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress for aid and tougher sanctions; US envoys Witkoff and Kushner want a deal by January. The EU stops buying Russian seaborne LNG from 1 January.
stories.market: Lower Russian refining tightens product markets (diesel and gasoline exports) more than crude; Europe's LNG ban removes about 12 million tonnes a year of supply, a support for TTF gas.

body: Ukraine's long-range campaign against Russian energy has resumed in force since Trump's mid-October energy truce lapsed. Reuters' sources put the hit to refinery runs at 45% since late October; Putin said gasoline prices have stabilised after an October peak and called for tighter security at energy sites.
Kyiv says it will stop only if Moscow halts attacks on Ukrainian energy. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha answered Putin's threat by telling him to end the war.

On diplomacy, Zelensky warned against a settlement at Ukraine's expense and complained about delays to Patriot interceptor deliveries. The EU's ban on Russian seaborne LNG from 1 January compares with about 11.8 million tonnes imported in the first ten months of this year.
The Bank of Russia set the official rate at 82.15 roubles per dollar for 24 November.

stories.headline: About 93,000 Displaced Reach Damazin as Fighting Spreads Across Sudan's Blue Nile State

Displacement is spreading to Roseires, Agadi and Al-Tadamun, with fighting reported in Kurmuk, Geissan, Wad Al-Mahi and Bau. The commission suspended emergency response rooms across the region and residents report shortages of food, water and shelter.

stories.headline: German Business Morale Rises to 90.6, Its Best Since May 2023, but Factories Lose Momentum
stories.summary: The Ifo business climate index rose to 90.6 in November from 90.1, matching forecasts and reaching its highest since May 2023. The current-conditions gauge rose to 89.4 and expectations to 91.9. Manufacturing sentiment fell to -1.2 from +0.9, its first setback after six monthly gains, while services jumped to +2.4. Trade (-16.3) and construction (-15.9) remain deeply negative.
stories.market: Supports the view that German growth is recovering into 2027, but the factory dip tempers the cyclical bid; the DAX fell 1.3% the same day on chip stocks.

body: Ifo's survey extended a run of improvement in German business sentiment, but the breakdown was mixed: services carried the gain while manufacturing turned down for the first time in seven months, even though November's flash PMI had shown factory output accelerating.
Expectations at 91.9 were just shy of the 92.0 forecast and the current assessment at 89.4 slightly below 89.5.

stories.headline: Brussels Flags 10 Governments Over Fiscal Rules and Moves to Fine Bulgaria, Months After It Joined the Euro
stories.summary: The European Commission on 24 Nov flagged 10 EU governments, including France, Belgium and Italy, for breaching fiscal rules, Valdis Dombrovskis said. Bulgaria is the only country facing a cash penalty, of up to €23 million, over a spending overshoot of 2.3% of GDP. France and Belgium, with deficits above 5% and debt above 110% of GDP, were given more time until a spring review. Germany was warned that its deficit is projected to rise from 4.1% this year to 4.5% in 2028, and 19 countries got extra leeway for defence spending.
stories.market: A reminder of fiscal strain in the euro core; OAT-Bund and BTP-Bund spreads widened 2bp and 4bp on Tuesday.

Chairman T V Narendran told CNBC-TV18 the company is reflecting on feedback about selling its steel tubes and colour businesses to APL Apollo, that talks continue on structuring the deal better, and that there are no plans to defer the agreement. He said Tata Steel remains confident of cutting debt.
stories.market: Shareholder pushback is now the key variable for both stocks; metal indices underperformed on a strong day for the Sensex.

body: The Rs 32,266 crore control deal announced last week has gone badly with investors in both companies. APL Apollo's slide on Wednesday took its two-session loss to roughly 37%.

stories.summary: Cipla received US FDA approval for the first generic version of GSK's Flovent asthma inhaler, co-developed with Teva, it said on 25 Nov. ABB India rose 2.5% to Rs 7,038 after its Swiss parent agreed to buy fan maker Ziehl-Abegg, and Shadowfax Technologies gained 2.4% on a deal to acquire intra-city logistics firm WeFast. stories.market: Respiratory generics are a margin driver for Indian pharma's US business; deal news supported mid-caps on a volatile day.

stories.headline: Yuan Touches a Three-Week High as the PBOC Sets Its Strongest Fix Since July 2022, Despite Tariff Threats
stories.summary: The onshore yuan rose to 6.6581 per dollar on Wednesday 25 Nov, its strongest since 2 Nov, and traded near 6.6659 at 03:05 GMT. The People's Bank of China set the midpoint at 6.7088, the strongest since July 2022 but 529 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, the widest weak-side gap since 3 Nov, a sign Beijing wants to slow the rally. Exporter dollar sales before Lunar New Year supported the currency even as Washington readied Section 301 tariffs.
stories.market: A managed, gradual yuan appreciation; the weaker-than-expected fixings signal the PBOC will lean against a fast move. Shanghai stocks fell about 1% with Asia's chip sell-off.

stories.headline: Hong Kong Bucks Asia's Rout as Chow Tai Fook Beats; Singapore's Current-Account Surplus Jumps to S$41.3 Billion
stories.summary: The Hang Seng closed Tuesday at 22,219.65 and rose as much as 1.3% on Wednesday, outperforming the region as its low exposure to chip stocks shielded it. Jeweller Chow Tai Fook's first-half net income beat estimates, though weaker margin guidance tempered the reaction. Singapore's third-quarter current-account surplus widened to S$41.31 billion from S$28.48 billion, and the STI closed up 0.1% at 4,958.87 on Tuesday.
stories.market: Hong Kong's relative resilience reflects its sector mix; Singapore's external surplus underpins the Singapore dollar.

stories.headline: Congress Lines Up Huang: Closed House Interviews on 1 December and a Public Senate Hearing on 3 December
stories.summary: Lawmakers from both parties vowed on 24 Nov to press Jensen Huang over reports involving an alleged Chinese spy, a former Megaspeed executive unrelated to him, and the diversion of advanced chips to China. Megaspeed, a Singapore company, and six other Southeast Asian firms are on a US trade blacklist. Senator Tom Cotton said Congress will pass bipartisan chip export-control bills; Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to say whether Huang is under investigation. Trump said he was personally involved in Huang's reinstatement.
stories.market: Headline risk for the S&P 500's largest weight: Nvidia fell about 6% on Tuesday after Monday's 31.5% surge; tighter export rules would weigh on Asian chip supply chains.

body: Huang's return has not ended the political story. Senators Chris Coons and Elizabeth Warren said they want answers on his role in sales of advanced AI chips, and the Justice Department would not confirm or deny a probe.
Nvidia added about $950 billion of market value on Monday, the largest one-day gain for any company on record, before giving back about 6% on Tuesday.

stories.summary: New York's Court of Appeals ruled 4-3 on 24 Nov that Google's YouTube, Meta's Instagram, Reddit and Snap are immune under Section 230 from claims that their platforms contributed to the 2022 Tops supermarket shooting in Buffalo. stories.summary: The UK sanctioned Yemen's Houthi movement and four of its officials on 24 Nov, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said, the same day a Houthi drone hit Riyadh's PIF Tower. The designations add to US and EU measures targeting the group's finances and procurement.

stories.summary: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission approved Calvary's acquisition of 14 Healthscope hospitals, ABC reported on 25 Nov, a step in the break-up of the private hospital operator.

stories.headline: Tehran's Open-Market Dollar Jumps About 5% to 2.82 Million Rials as Blockade Pressure Mounts
stories.summary: The US dollar traded at about 2.82 million rials in Tehran's open market on Tuesday afternoon 24 Nov, up roughly 5% from about 2.68 million, and the euro at about 3.07 million from 2.94 million, Gulf News reported. The move came a day after US Treasury sanctions on an Iranian shadow-banking network of exchange houses, including the Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold.
stories.market: The widening gap between official and street rates tracks Iran's loss of oil revenue under the blockade; it is a real-time gauge of sanctions pressure.

stories.headline: FinCEN Flags $14.7 Billion of Possible Iran-Linked Flows as Washington Warns Ship-to-Ship Buyers Over Blockade Evasion
stories.summary: Alongside Monday's sanctions on 22 entities and 8 people in an Iranian shadow-banking network spanning Iran, Dubai, Hong Kong and Turkey, FinCEN said it had identified about $14.7 billion in potentially Iran-linked activity between January 2025 and August 2026. US Central Command has separately warned that vessels receiving cargo from ships loaded at Iranian ports may be evading the blockade.
stories.market: Raises secondary-sanctions risk for Gulf and Asian banks, money-service businesses and tanker owners handling ship-to-ship transfers.

stories.headline: Justice Department Says Its Record Scam Crackdown Has Reached More Than 800 Defendants and $1 Billion-Plus in Restrained Crypto
stories.summary: The DOJ said on 24 Nov that its largest-ever anti-scam push has charged more than 800 defendants in over 400 cases across 85 districts since 6 March 2026, with 30 extradited. Its Scam Center Strike Force has traced and restrained more than $1.08 billion of crypto stolen from US victims, including $52 million restrained in one day when it seized Telegram channels used by Xinbi Guarantee. The FBI's Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion and dismantled more than 29 scam compounds. Americans lost an estimated $68 billion to scams in 2025, Gallup estimates.
stories.market: Heightened enforcement on stablecoin rails (USDT flows) and Southeast Asian scam networks raises compliance costs for exchanges and banks in the region.

stories.headline: DOJ Files to Forfeit $1.1 Billion of USDC From the Binance Heist; More Than $2.9 Billion Now Frozen, Seized or Returned
stories.summary: The Justice Department filed a civil action on 24 Nov to permanently forfeit more than $1.1 billion of USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance on 29 Oct, part of a theft exceeding $6 billion attributed to the TraderTraitor group. US authorities and partners have now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion tied to the hack, with stablecoin issuer Circle assisting. The FBI, Secret Service and IRS-CI are leading the investigation.
stories.market: Shows issuer-level freezes on regulated stablecoins can claw back stolen funds, a selling point for USDC; less than half of the stolen sum has been recovered.

stories.headline: Sanofi Agrees to Buy Insmed for $41 Billion in Cash, the Biggest Pharma Deal Since Pfizer-Seagen
stories.summary: Sanofi agreed on 24 Nov to acquire Insmed for $175 a share in cash, valuing the respiratory and immunology drugmaker at about $41 billion. The price is a 26% premium to Monday's close (Reuters cited about 17.5% on a different reference) and 46% above the price before Bloomberg first reported Sanofi's interest on 19 Nov. Sanofi expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027 and to add to earnings per share by the end of 2028. Sanofi shares rose 9.9% in Paris; Truist puts the break fee at about $1.125 billion.
stories.market: A vote of confidence in large-cap pharma as a defensive growth trade: Lilly rose 3%, J&J nearly 2% and Alnylam more than 5.5% on read-across.

body: The deal gives Sanofi Insmed's Arikayce and Brinsupri, the latter cleared in 2025 for non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis. The two drugs brought in $524 million in the third quarter and Insmed has guided to as much as $1.87 billion of 2026 revenue; Jefferies' consensus sees Brinsupri reaching $6.8 billion by 2035.

At about $41 billion it is the year's largest biopharma acquisition by roughly $30 billion and the biggest since Pfizer paid $43 billion for Seagen in 2023. The offer is still about 17% below Insmed's December 2025 peak of $211.

Analysts see little room for a counterbid: Truist says credible rivals are scarce. Oppenheimer noted Sanofi could have bought Alnylam instead, and BMO's Evan Seigerman tied the timing to a rotation into pharma amid the Nvidia turmoil.

stories.market: Large blocks at a discount typically signal a stake sale; overhang risk for the stock until the parties are known.

stories.headline: Dell Doubles Revenue to $54.9 Billion on AI Servers, Lifts Its Outlook and Adds a $25 Billion Buyback
stories.summary: Dell's fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 103% to $54.94 billion, against about $49.3 billion expected, and adjusted EPS was $9.45 versus $6.59, it reported on 24 Nov. AI-optimised server sales jumped 291% to $22.0 billion, the AI backlog reached $132.3 billion after $60.2 billion of bookings, and it raised its full-year AI server outlook to $78 billion. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance is $56.3 billion. The board approved an extra $25 billion buyback. The stock fell 11% in the regular session before rising about 1-3% after hours.
stories.market: A blowout from the AI hardware chain on a day the sector sold off; PC and client sales ($12.9bn, a miss) remain the soft spot.

stories.headline: HP Beats on Sales and Profit but Its Cash-Flow Guide Disappoints, Erasing a 17% After-Hours Jump
stories.summary: HP's fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of $0.83 beat the $0.75 consensus and revenue rose 9% to $16.0 billion against $15.4 billion expected, it said on 24 Nov. It gave no EPS guidance and forecast current-quarter free cash flow of about $3 billion, below the $3.3 billion analysts targeted, as margins narrowed. The shares rose more than 17% after hours before giving it all back and ending about 1-3% lower. Emma Walmsley takes over as CEO on 4 January.
stories.market: PC makers are being squeezed by AI-driven component costs; the reaction shows how little benefit of the doubt hardware names get this week.

stories.headline: Analog Devices Sinks 17% Despite a Record Quarter as Its Outlook Shows Growth Stalling
stories.summary: Analog Devices fell 17.37% to $312.95 on 24 Nov after fiscal fourth-quarter EPS of $4.06 (up 80%) and revenue of $4.37 billion (up 42%) beat estimates of about $3.89 and $4.32 billion. Its first-quarter outlook matched consensus but implied a sequential slowdown, with margins squeezed by component costs and holiday fab shutdowns. Plants are running at full capacity, capex is up 150% and new lines will not produce until the second half of 2028; it plans $1.6-1.9 billion of capital spending next year.
stories.market: Analog and industrial chipmakers (Texas Instruments, Microchip, NXP, Infineon) traded lower on read-across.

stories.headline: Dollar Tree Jumps 11% and Kohl's 19% as Both Beat and Raise Into the Holidays
stories.summary: Dollar Tree's third-quarter sales rose 6.9% to $5.07 billion and comparable sales 4.6%, above the top of its outlook, with adjusted EPS of $1.16 including 42 cents of tariff reinvestment costs, it said on 24 Nov. It raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $8.05-8.25 and guided fourth-quarter sales to $5.7-5.8 billion; the stock rose 11.18%. Kohl's surged 19.48% after an earnings beat.
stories.market: Value retail is winning share as consumers trade down; the gains fed Tuesday's rotation into consumer and defensive stocks.

stories.headline: Six Brokers Downgrade Zscaler After CrowdStrike's All-Stock Bid, While Guggenheim Upgrades CrowdStrike to Buy
stories.summary: Bernstein (to Market Perform), Capital One (Equal Weight), Jefferies, Stifel and TD Cowen (Hold) and Rosenblatt (Neutral) all cut Zscaler on 24 Nov, effectively moving to deal-arbitrage stances after CrowdStrike's $43.9 billion all-stock offer. DA Davidson went the other way, upgrading Zscaler to Buy. Guggenheim raised CrowdStrike to Buy from Neutral after the shares fell about 9% on the announcement.
stories.market: Zscaler now trades on the exchange ratio and CrowdStrike's share price; arbitrage spreads will reflect antitrust and shareholder-vote risk.

stories.headline: BNP Cuts Micron, HSBC Cuts Intuit; Mizuho Starts Defence Primes at Outperform and Seaport Launches on Autos
stories.summary: BNP Paribas downgraded Micron to Neutral from Outperform and HSBC cut Intuit to Hold from Buy on 24 Nov; Micron then fell 11% in the chip sell-off. Mizuho initiated Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris and Boeing at Outperform, and Rocket Lab and Redwire at Underperform. Seaport began Tesla, GM, Ford and Rivian at Buy and Lucid at Sell. BofA double-upgraded Burberry to Buy from Underperform.
stories.market: Defence primes get fresh sponsorship as conflicts spread; memory chips lose a bull just as the AI trade wobbles.

stories.headline: Ibovespa Slips to Its Lowest Close in Six Months as Vale Slides 5.5% With Copper and Iron Ore
stories.summary: The Ibovespa fell 0.43% to 164,089.81 on 24 Nov, a fourth straight loss and the lowest close in at least six months, leaving it 21.5% below its 9 Oct peak. Vale dropped 5.51% and Petrobras 1.82%; the real firmed 0.4% to 5.9066 per dollar. The economic team is drafting a spending-restraint constitutional amendment for President Lula, with scope and timing not yet set.
stories.market: Commodity-heavy Brazil is caught in the copper and iron-ore slide; the fiscal amendment is the domestic swing factor for the real and DI rates.

stories.headline: Peso Falls for a Fifth Day to Its Weakest in 12 Months as Mid-November Inflation Tops Forecasts
stories.summary: The peso weakened 1.21% to 19.41 per dollar on 24 Nov, its fifth straight loss and weakest close in a year, after mid-November headline inflation of 3.96% beat the 3.92% forecast, though core eased to 3.68%. The IPC index still rose 0.83% to 69,932.54, led by Alpek (+7.4%) and airport operator GAP (+4.2%), while Grupo Mexico fell about 5%.
stories.market: A narrowing US-Mexico rate gap as the Fed hikes is eroding the peso's carry appeal.

stories.headline: Loonie Rises 0.7%, Leading Commodity Currencies, After Macklem Warns on Inflation
stories.summary: The Canadian dollar gained about 0.7% against the US dollar on 24 Nov after Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem warned about inflation, Saxo reported, outperforming most G10 currencies on a day the dollar index slipped 0.2%.
stories.market: Hawkish central-bank talk supports the loonie and Canadian short-end yields.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 Holds Near 10,467 as Miners Fall and the CBI's Retail Gauge Turns Positive
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 edged 0.1% lower to 10,467.07 on 24 Nov, with Antofagasta down 8.1% on copper's slide offset by defensive stocks. The CBI's retail sales balance came in at +9, and gilt yields fell 1-3bp.
stories.market: London's defensive, low-tech mix kept it steadier than the DAX; miners are the drag.

stories.headline: Saudi Stocks Edge Up 0.4% to 9,977 Despite a Second Houthi Strike on Riyadh's PIF Tower
stories.summary: The TASI rose 39.8 points, or 0.4%, to 9,977.06 on 24 Nov on turnover of SR2.99 billion, with 151 gainers and 104 losers; the Nomu parallel market added 0.38% to 21,325. The gains came on the day a Houthi drone hit the PIF Tower in Riyadh for the second time in five days.
stories.market: Local investors looked through the attack, but the index remains below 10,000 and Red Sea port threats are a new risk for Saudi logistics names.

stories.headline: Nigeria Holds Its Policy Rate at 23% Unanimously as Inflation Eases to 14.06%
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's MPC kept the rate at 23% in a unanimous vote on 24 Nov, leaving the corridor at +50/-300bp and cash-reserve ratios at 45% for commercial banks. Headline inflation eased to 14.06% in October from 14.63%. The naira weakened to N1,394.01 per dollar on Monday, and analysts flagged pre-election spending as a risk to disinflation.
stories.market: A hold keeps Nigerian T-bill yields deeply positive in real terms, supporting carry flows into the naira.

stories.headline: Rand Firms About 0.8% to 17.54 per Dollar as the JSE Top-40 Slips
stories.summary: The rand traded at 17.5399 per dollar at 14:03 GMT on 24 Nov, about 0.8% stronger as the dollar softened, while the JSE Top-40 fell about 0.6%. The 2035 government bond yield was little changed at 8.665%, and September's leading indicator fell 0.3% m/m.
stories.market: The rand tracks the global dollar and US rate path; PCE is the next driver.

stories.headline: Central Bank Sets the Rouble Slightly Firmer at 82.15 per Dollar as Refinery Strikes Squeeze Fuel Supply
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia set official rates for 24 Nov at 82.1488 roubles per dollar, 90.2815 per euro and 12.2615 per yuan, each slightly firmer. Reuters sources say Ukrainian drone strikes have cut refinery throughput by 45% since late October, and several regions restrict retail fuel sales.
stories.market: A stable rouble masks pressure on domestic fuel markets; lower refining raises Russia's crude export availability.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea Expected to Hike to 3.25% on Thursday as Exports Double and the Kospi Whipsaws
stories.summary: All ten local brokerages surveyed expect a 25bp hike to 3.25% on 26 Nov, with most seeing a 3.50% peak. Exports in the first 20 days of November doubled (+101.5%) to a record $77.4 billion, half of it chips. The Kospi jumped 6.32% to 5,006.03 on Tuesday, then fell about 6.5% on Wednesday; the won closed Tuesday at 1,342.4 per dollar.
stories.market: A hike plus extreme equity volatility puts the won and Korean bond yields (3-year 3.64%) in focus.

stories.headline: Taiex Falls Up to 7.9% as TSMC and Foxconn Drop More Than 9%, a Day After Its Record Point Gain
stories.summary: Taiwan's Taiex fell as much as 7.9% on Wednesday morning, with TSMC and Foxconn each down more than 9%, reversing Tuesday's biggest-ever intraday point gain. The market is operating under short-selling curbs introduced after its worst week since 2001.
stories.market: The Taiex is the purest listed proxy for AI hardware demand; the Taiwan dollar is exposed to any resumption of foreign outflows.

stories.headline: Inflation Jumps to 4.9% on Electricity and Fuel, but Markets Still Bet the RBA Holds in December
stories.summary: Australia's October CPI rose 4.9% y/y, up from 4.3% and above the 4.8% forecast, as electricity rose 25.2% with rebates expiring and fuel 32.5%; the trimmed mean rose to 3.8%. The ASX 200 fell 0.4% to 8,692 and the Australian dollar eased to 65.91 US cents. Markets price about a 97% chance of no change at the RBA's 8 Dec meeting.
stories.market: Hotter inflation keeps further RBA hikes on the table for 2027, supporting short-end yields; the 10-year traded near 4.84%.

stories.headline: Services Prices Rise at the Fastest Pace Since 1990 as the Nikkei Drops About 2.8% With Chip Stocks
stories.summary: Japan's services producer price index rose 4.2% y/y in October, up from 3.8% and the fastest since 1990, strengthening the case for a BOJ hike. The Nikkei 225, which closed Tuesday at 58,644.63, fell about 2.8% on Wednesday as Tokyo Electron dropped 13.5% and Advantest 14.5%. The yen held just above 159 per dollar.
stories.market: Rising service inflation supports JGB yields and the yen; chip-equipment makers dominate the index's downside.
